channel.title: OpenRouter Blog
channel.description: Latest posts and updates from OpenRouter.

item.title: Private Endpoints: Bring Your Fine-Tuned Models and Capacity to OpenRouter
item.description: Private Endpoints let Enterprise customers route their own fine-tuned models and dedicated deployments through OpenRouter, alongside the public catalog. Private endpoints are only visible within your organization, and requests go through the API your team already uses. Available by request on the Enterprise plan.

item.title: ElevenLabs is now on OpenRouter
item.description: ElevenLabs is now on OpenRouter with 9 Text to Speech and 2 Speech to Text models. Deliver speech with human-like emotion with Eleven v4, give your agent low-latency replies with v4 Turbo, and turn meetings into notes that show who said what with Scribe v2. Here's which model to pick, and one project built start to finish.

item.title: How an AI Sales Agent Saved Our Sales Team 600 Hours a Month
item.description: Rasp gives OpenRouter's five-person sales team about 600 hours a month back, adds room for two more calls a day per rep, and runs for about $30 a day on Ori.

item.title: Server-Side Code Execution Tools for AI Agents, Compared
item.description: A server-side code execution tool runs the model's commands in the provider's sandbox during your API request, so you don't provision or secure a container. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google run code for their own models. Our openrouter:shell tool runs commands for any model on the Responses and Messages APIs, and our openrouter:bash tool does the same on the Messages API. This article compares the four on runtime, isolation, persistence, and cost, shows a complete request against our sandbox with the output it returned, and describes the jobs that still need a sandbox platform of your own.

item.title: Agent Frameworks Compared: Tool-Calling Schema Handling
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google each use a different request and response shape for the same tool. Agent frameworks handle that difference in different places. Some translate one definition into each provider's format, some are native to a single provider, and some hand the question to a connector underneath. This article compares six frameworks on schema definition, translation, and MCP support, then shows how OpenRouter normalizes tool calling at the API layer so a model swap is a change to one string.

item.title: LangChain vs CrewAI: Orchestration Compared to OpenRouter-Native Routing
item.description: Multi-model orchestration is three layers. Workflow orchestration is planning, state, memory, and delegation, and LangGraph and CrewAI are built for it. Model routing is choosing a model per call and falling back when it fails, and provider routing is choosing which provider serves that model. OpenRouter does the second two. This article separates the layers, shows the same two-step pipeline in direct OpenRouter calls and in LangChain, and describes when to add a framework, when to use our Agent SDK, and how to put OpenRouter underneath LangGraph or CrewAI.

item.title: Model Router Benchmarks
item.description: We now benchmark model routers side by side across six suites. Our Router Index weighs quality, speed, and cost so you can decide if you need a router and pick the best one for your needs.

item.title: Model Routing for Support Bots: Cheap-First FAQ Handling
item.description: Cheap-first routing sends routine support questions to a small, inexpensive model and escalates selected hard or uncertain requests to a stronger one. This guide compares the three application-side routing patterns, separates what your application owns from what OpenRouter's Auto Router and model fallbacks handle, walks through a support flow with a copyable request, and sets out how to measure escalation rate and cost per resolved ticket.

item.title: Confidence Thresholds for Model Escalation Routing
item.description: Confidence-based escalation keeps most requests on a cheap model and sends only the ones it is unsure about to a stronger one. This guide covers forcing a numeric confidence field with structured outputs, setting the threshold from error rates on your own traffic, tuning it against accuracy, cost, and latency, routing the escalation in your code, and re-tuning it after launch.

item.title: Cost vs. Quality Tradeoff Framework for Agent Models
item.description: The cheapest model that clears your quality bar is usually not the model at the top of a leaderboard. This framework sets the bar for one task, measures cost per quality point across a cheap, a mid-tier, and a frontier model on your own examples, and picks the cheapest one that clears the bar with margin. It uses live catalog prices and the cost each OpenRouter response reports.

item.title: How to Gate Pull Requests on LLM Evals in CI
item.description: A one-line prompt change can ship an agent that tells customers the wrong refund window, and nothing in a normal CI pipeline checks what the model says. This guide builds a fixed eval set for a support agent, a script that exits non-zero below a measured threshold, and a GitHub Actions job that blocks the merge when the pass rate drops.

item.title: AI Agent Regression Testing After a Prompt or Model Change
item.description: An agent's behavior can change when you edit a prompt, swap a model, change a tool schema, or change what retrieval returns. This guide covers the locked case set, the per-case behavioral contract, and how to run the same suite against two concrete model slugs through OpenRouter so the diff shows what the change did.
